items.title: Charles Tolliver interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 6, 2021 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I didn’t get a chance for any of us guys to rub shoulders together so to speak, during that period.

ctx.x: I’ve been reading a little bit about Sun Ra and that — I guess very experimental music that he did and others at that time. I wonder if you had any experience hearing him or groups like the Art Ensemble of Chicago, that were — I mean they were out there I guess is the best way I can put it. And I’m wondering if you’d ever heard them live?

No, except for, you know of course Sun Ra, because I was coming up at the same time as when he was really at the forefront of what he was doing. But I didn’t get a chance for any of us guys to rub shoulders together so to speak, during that period. But they carved out a niche in this and, you know, a lot of it had to do with musical theater. You know? Which struck a lot of fans as very interesting and palatable and so rather than coming to a performance in bow tie you know, they would come to hear these fellows…
